session.question: In hepatocellular carcinoma, what was found about macrophage migration inhibitory factor, and how did its knockdown affect tumor cell behavior and related protein expression?
session.answer:
Macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) was significantly upregulated in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tissues and cell lines relative to adjacent normal liver tissues or a normal liver cell line. In HCC specimens, MIF expression correlated positively with cyclin D1 expression and tumor size, consistent with a role in tumor growth. (huang2014smallinterferingrna chunk 1)

siRNA-mediated MIF knockdown inhibited proliferation of PLC and HepG2 HCC cells, promoted apoptosis, and reduced tumor growth in a xenograft model, but did not alter cell-cycle distribution. Mechanistically, MIF depletion decreased cyclin D1, p-Akt, and p-ERK, while increasing Bcl-2, p-caspase-3, BIM, and Bax, indicating suppression of growth and survival signaling with activation of apoptotic pathways. (huang2014smallinterferingrna chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-7ee9b51b: The study found that macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) was significantly upregulated in hepatocellular carcinoma tissues and cell lines compared with adjacent normal tissues or a normal liver cell line. In HCC specimens, MIF expression positively correlated with cyclin D1 expression and tumor size. Knocking down MIF with siRNA inhibited proliferation of PLC and HepG2 cells, promoted apoptosis, and reduced tumor growth in a xenograft model. It did not affect the cell cycle. MIF knockdown also increased Bcl-2, p-caspase-3, BIM, and Bax, while decreasing cyclin D1, p-Akt, and p-ERK, suggesting MIF supports growth and survival signaling in HCC.
From Xiao-hui Huang, Wei-hua Jian, Zhao-feng Wu, Jie Zhao, Hua Wang, Wen Li, and Jin-tang Xia. Small interfering rna (sirna)-mediated knockdown of macrophage migration inhibitory factor (mif) suppressed cyclin d1 expression and hepatocellular carcinoma cell proliferation. Oncotarget, 2014. URL: https://doi.org/10.18632/oncotarget.2141, doi:10.18632/oncotarget.2141.

pqac-24fbb756: The excerpt is about P27RF-Rho in hepatocellular carcinoma, not macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF). It reports that lentivirus-mediated knockdown of P27RF-Rho inhibited HCC cell growth and colony formation, caused cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis, and changed expression of growth/apoptosis/metastasis-related genes: cyclin A, CDK2, BCL-2, and MMP-9 were down-regulated, while P27 and Bax were up-regulated. No information about MIF is provided in this excerpt.
From Shuli Xie, Guangyi Wang, Guofu Chen, Mingguang Zhu, and Guoyue Lv. Lentivirus-mediated knockdown of p27rf-rho inhibits hepatocellular carcinoma cell growth. Contemporary Oncology, 2017. URL: https://doi.org/10.5114/wo.2017.66654, doi:10.5114/wo.2017.66654.

pqac-4d2d7a11: The excerpt is about GFAT1 in hepatocellular carcinoma, not macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF). It reports that high GFAT1 expression was associated with worse clinicopathologic features (AFP, ALT, tumor size, encapsulation, T stage, TNM stage) and independently predicted poor overall survival and recurrence-free survival. GFAT1 also improved prognostic accuracy when added to TNM staging, and in vitro it promoted HCC cell proliferation, cell cycle progression, migration, and invasion. The excerpt does not mention MIF, its knockdown, or related protein-expression changes.
From Lili Li, Miaomiao Shao, Peike Peng, Caiting Yang, Shushu Song, Fangfang Duan, Dongwei Jia, Mingming Zhang, Junjie Zhao, Ran Zhao, Weicheng Wu, Lan Wang, Can Li, Hao Wu, Jie Zhang, Xin Wu, Yuanyuan Ruan, and Jianxin Gu. High expression of gfat1 predicts unfavorable prognosis in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma. Oncotarget, 2017. URL: https://doi.org/10.18632/oncotarget.15164, doi:10.18632/oncotarget.15164.

pqac-1b684901: The excerpt is about BAP31 and doxorubicin resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma, not macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF). It reports that BAP31 was overexpressed in Dox-resistant HCC cells; knocking down BAP31 lowered the IC50, increased Dox-induced apoptosis, and improved chemosensitivity in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, BAP31 promoted FoxO1 nucleus-cytoplasm translocation and thereby inhibited survivin expression; BAP31 and survivin knockdown together had a synergistic pro-apoptotic effect. No information about MIF, its knockdown, tumor cell behavior, or its protein expression is included in this excerpt.
From Jingjing Liu, Qi Zhang, Changli Wang, Jiaying Yang, Sheng Yang, Tianyi Wang, and Bing Wang. Knockdown of bap31 overcomes hepatocellular carcinoma doxorubicin resistance through downregulation of survivin. International Journal of Molecular Sciences, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms24087622, doi:10.3390/ijms24087622.

pqac-c955c9b5: The excerpt is about ROCK/RhoA signaling in hepatocellular carcinoma vasculogenic mimicry, not macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF). It reports that HCC cells with higher active RhoA/ROCK were more prone to form VM channels, while the ROCK inhibitor Y27632 dose-dependently inhibited tubular network formation, migration, and invasion. ROCK blockade also reduced expression of VM-related factors (VE-cadherin, EphA2, PI3K, MMP14, MMP2, MMP9, LAMC2) and EMT markers (E-cadherin, Vimentin). No information about MIF or MIF knockdown is provided in this excerpt.
From Ji-Gang Zhang, Xiao-Yu Li, Yu-Zhu Wang, Qi-Di Zhang, Sheng-Ying Gu, Xin Wu, Guan-Hua Zhu, Qin Li, and Gao-Lin Liu. Rock is involved in vasculogenic mimicry formation in hepatocellular carcinoma cell line. PLoS ONE, 2014. URL: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0107661, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0107661.

Question: In hepatocellular carcinoma, what was found about macrophage migration inhibitory factor, and how did its knockdown affect tumor cell behavior and related protein expression?

Macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) was significantly upregulated in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tissues and cell lines relative to adjacent normal liver tissues or a normal liver cell line. In HCC specimens, MIF expression correlated positively with cyclin D1 expression and tumor size, consistent with a role in tumor growth. (huang2014smallinterferingrna chunk 1)

siRNA-mediated MIF knockdown inhibited proliferation of PLC and HepG2 HCC cells, promoted apoptosis, and reduced tumor growth in a xenograft model, but did not alter cell-cycle distribution. Mechanistically, MIF depletion decreased cyclin D1, p-Akt, and p-ERK, while increasing Bcl-2, p-caspase-3, BIM, and Bax, indicating suppression of growth and survival signaling with activation of apoptotic pathways. (huang2014smallinterferingrna chunk 1)
